We need retrosynthesis of target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Looks like a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings, one with para-methyl (p-tolyl) sulfonyl attached to another phenyl bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl anilide). So we can think disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. So precursor A: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-CH3C6H4SO2Cl) and precursor B: aniline bearing the cinnamoyl amide (i.e., 4-((E)-3-(phenylamido)acryloyl)aniline?). Actually the sulfonamide attaches to an aniline (the second aromatic ring). The second aromatic ring has a para substituent of the cinnamoyl amide. So we could have 4-aminophenyl with that substituent, then sulfonylation.

Thus step1: sulfonylation of aniline with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride.

Precursors: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and 4-((E)-3-(phenylamido)acryloyl)aniline (maybe not commercial). Could further disconnect the amide formation: the amide between aniline (cinnamoyl) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (anilide). So we can form amide via coupling of 4-((E)-3-(phenylamido)acrylic acid?) Wait: The fragment is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. That's an α,β-unsaturated amide where the carbonyl attached to an aniline (anilide). So we could make that via condensation of trans-cinnamic acid derivative with aniline (aniline). But the double bond is conjugated to carbonyl; we could start from trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and couple with aniline to give trans-cinnamamide (C=O-NH-Ph). Then we need to attach that cinnamamide to the para position of the second phenyl via a Suzuki coupling? Actually the structure: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group at para position? The sulfonyl attaches to the aniline nitrogen of that ring (the second ring). The second ring is phenyl with para substituent of the cinnamamide (attached via carbon at para). So we need to attach the cinnamamide to the phenyl ring via a C-C bond at para position. That could be via Heck coupling of iodo-phenyl sulfonamide with trans-cinnamyl? But maybe easier: start from 4-bromo-phenyl sulfonamide (the sulfonamide after step1) and do Suzuki coupling with trans-cinnamyl boronic acid? However the double bond is conjugated to carbonyl; we could use Heck coupling of 4-iodophenyl sulfonamide with trans-cinnamyl acrylate? Might be complex.

Alternative: Disconnection at the C=C bond: break to give aldehyde and amide? Not.

Simplify: Use three steps max. Could propose:

Step1: Form amide: React trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) with aniline (commercial) using coupling reagent (e.g., EDC) to give trans-cinnamamide (C=O-NH-Ph). That's step1.

Step2: Perform Suzuki coupling between 4-bromo-phenyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl chloride with bromo) and the trans-cinnamamide phenyl boronic acid? Wait we need to attach the cinnamamide to phenyl ring. Could use Suzuki coupling of 4-bromo phenyl sulfonyl chloride with phenylboronic acid that already has the cinnamamide attached? Actually we could have 4-bromo phenyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial?) maybe not. Another route: start from 4-iodophenyl sulfonyl chloride (commercial) and do Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(phenylamido)styryl boronic acid (the cinnamamide phenyl attached to double bond). That boronic acid may not be commercial.

Maybe better: Use a Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach the cinnamoyl amide onto phenyl after sulfonamide formation? But Friedel-Crafts on aniline is problematic.

Given constraints, maybe we can propose a route using three steps with commercially available building blocks:

- Building block 1: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) (commercial)
- Building block 2: 4-aminophenyl (para-aminophenyl) with the cinnamamide already attached? Not commercial.

But we could use 4-aminobenzaldehyde (commercial) to do Knoevenagel condensation with benzamide? Not.

Maybe we can propose a convergent route: Step A: Synthesize the sulfonamide from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) (commercial). That gives p-tolyl sulfonyl aniline (p-tolylSO2NH-Ph-NH2). Then we need to acylate the second amine (para position) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (derived from trans-cinnamic acid). So step2: Acylation of the aniline (the second ring) with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give the amide. That yields final product? Wait the final product has the amide attached to the phenyl via carbonyl attached to the phenyl (C=O attached to phenyl). In our intermediate, we have sulfonamide attached to aniline (NH2). The aniline's NH2 is free; we need to convert it to amide with trans-cinnamoyl chloride, but the amide in target is attached to the phenyl carbon, not nitrogen. Actually the target: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The phenyl ring (c2) has a substituent that is a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached via carbon (C=O attached to phenyl). So the phenyl is attached to carbonyl carbon (aryl-CO-). So it's an aryl ketone? Wait structure: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph. The phenyl ring is attached to the carbonyl carbon via C=O (aryl carbonyl). So the phenyl is part of the amide carbonyl side: it's an anilide where the carbonyl carbon is attached to phenyl (aryl amide). So the phenyl ring is the carbonyl's aryl group, not the amine side. The amine side is another phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached to the amide nitrogen. So the amide is between trans-alkene carbonyl and an aniline (anilide). The phenyl bearing the sulfonamide is attached to the carbonyl carbon (aryl acyl). So we need to have aryl acyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl aniline?) Actually the aryl carbonyl is the phenyl that also bears the sulfonamide substituent. So we need to have that phenyl with sulfonamide and a carbonyl substituent (acyl chloride) to react with aniline.

Thus route:

Step1: Prepare sulfonamide phenyl with para-acyl chloride: start from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) and 4-aminobenzoyl chloride? Not.

Better: Start from 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually we need phenyl that has both sulfonamide (SO2NH-) and a carbonyl (COCl) para to each other. Could be synthesized by sulfonylation of 4-aminobenzoyl chloride (p-aminobenzoyl chloride) with TsCl? Wait p-aminobenzoyl chloride is 4-aminobenzoyl chloride (ClCO-Ph-NH2). Sulfonylation of the amine with TsCl would give p-tolylSO2NH-CO-Ph? That would attach sulfonyl to the amine, not to the phenyl. In target, sulfonamide nitrogen attached to phenyl (p-tolyl) and the phenyl bearing sulfonamide is attached via nitrogen to sulfonyl group, not carbonyl. So the phenyl bearing sulfonamide is the p-tolyl group (CH3-Ph-SO2-). The other phenyl (the one with carbonyl) is the second phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl (the one with carbonyl). So the second phenyl has both sulfonamide (via N) and carbonyl substituent (via C). So we need to have an aniline (the second phenyl) that is sulfonylated (forming sulfonamide) and also acylated (forming aryl ketone). The order can be either.

Thus we can start with 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) (commercial). Step1: Sulfonylate the amine with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride to give p-tolylSO2NH-Ph-NH2 (sulfonamide). Step2: Acylate the aromatic ring (para to sulfonamide?) Actually the amine is now sulfonamide, the aromatic ring still has a free position para to the sulfonamide (the original para position relative to the sulfonamide nitrogen? In the target, the carbonyl substituent is para to the sulfonamide nitrogen on the same phenyl. So we need to introduce a carbonyl group at para position of the sulfonamide phenyl. That can be done via Friedel-Crafts acylation of the sulfonamide phenyl with trans-cinnamoyl chloride? However Friedel-Crafts on aniline is deactivated by sulfonamide? Might be possible with strong Lewis acid.

Alternative: Use Suzuki coupling to attach the cinnamoyl aryl group. Could start from 4-bromo-phenyl sulfonamide (commercial?) maybe not.

Given time, maybe we can propose a plausible route using three steps and assume commercial availability of key intermediates: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, 4-aminophenylboronic acid, trans-cinnamoyl chloride, and aniline. But need to ensure leaves are commercially available.

Simplify: Provide route:

Step1: Sulfonylation: p-toluenesulfonyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) -> sulfonamide (intermediate A).

Step2: Suzuki coupling: Intermediate A (as aryl bromide at para position) with (E)-3-(phenylamido)styryl boronic acid (commercial? maybe not). Not good.

Maybe we can propose a different disconnection: Break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde and amide? Could do Wittig to form double bond later. So we could have aryl ketone (aryl-CO-NH-Ph) as intermediate, then perform Wittig to install the trans-alkene. That could be step2: Wittig reaction between aryl ketone and phosphonium ylide derived from (CH2) etc. But Wittig reagents not commercial as SMILES? Could be.

Given constraints, maybe we can produce a plausible route with three steps using commercially available reagents, even if some are not typical but assume they are.

We need to produce JSON with reactions and template IDs. We need template IDs; we can search for templates for sulfonylation, amide formation, Wittig.

Let's search for sulfonylation template.
